select.$description: Closed dropdown trigger — same box model as component.input (sm has no floating label; base/lg float a 12px label above the 16px selected-value once a choice is made or the trigger is focused). Always shows a trailing chevron. Opens a Listbox under the field (2026-10-26: a real <button aria-haspopup=listbox> + popover listbox in tools/lib/select.mjs, keyboard included). States: focus (active, closed) vs open (list showing, chevron up). Error: required and nothing chosen on Submit, or a choice that no longer works (e.g. the section filled up, the advisor isn't free that day) — border.dangerStrong plus the Field message. Multiple: the field shows the first choice + a Counter for the rest ('Email  +2'); a field that lists every choice as removable chips is MultiSelectBadges (Fields, later).

value.$description: 14px at every size (was 16px until 2026-10-07). Select is a button that opens the Listbox — not a native <select> and never a text field — so the iOS Safari focus-zoom that forces 16px on Input/Search does not apply; the live product's Select (Radix, role=combobox, text-sm) is 14px too. Implement it as a button + Listbox; a native <select> on iOS would need 16px again.

size.$description: Identical to component.input.size — same reasoning, see that token's own $description.

focus.$description: Same as input.state.focus — keyboard focus on the trigger, before/without the menu necessarily being open.

open.$description: The list is showing (aria-expanded=true). Same border and label as focus, plus the chevron turned up — focus alone means the field is active but closed (arrived by Tab). Added 2026-10-26.

populated.$description: Has a chosen value — label stays floated, colors revert to default.

more.$description: The '+N' after the first choice in a multiple Select. Counter's size (counter.size.sm), but its own colours: counter.onNeutral's gray.300 is made to stand out on Tabs' gray.100 track and read as a heavy blot inside a gray.50 field (user, 2026-10-27). bg.neutralStrong (gray.150) — the neutral Badge tint — with text.secondary keeps it a quiet aside to the value.
